Regular workspace files are copied byte for byte, regardless of type or extension, to a location chosen in Android’s document picker. Alternatively, the ZIP contains all regular files with their relative directory structure. Symbolic links, hard links, outside paths, and the separate CODEX_HOME are never exported.

Codex owns discovery and configuration. AGENTCODI never reads config.toml or marketplace files and never exposes response file paths. This screen may write only the validated user MCP-server subset through config/read, config/batchWrite, and config/mcpServer/reload; tool invocation, authentication, connector installation, marketplace mutation, credential fields, and all other configuration remain unavailable.

Expert feature: changes affect the Codex user configuration. New servers are always saved disabled first. Every edit and enable action fixes the server default to prompt and removes per-tool approval overrides, so no tool can bypass its native decision dialog. Review the entry, then enable it explicitly. Static environment variables, HTTP headers, bearer-token settings, OAuth, and direct configuration-file access are intentionally unavailable.

OpenAI Codex 0.148.1 and the Android/Termux community distribution · Apache License 2.0. This is not an official OpenAI Android APK.

Node.js LTS 24.18.0 and its pinned Android runtime dependencies · bundled in the APK and enabled only by an explicit user action or approved Codex command. Includes MIT, Unicode-3.0, Apache-2.0, zlib, and public-domain components.
npm 11.19.0 and its bundled dependency licenses · runs through the pinned Node.js runtime and uses only workspace/toolchain for writable cache and prefix data.

Python 3.14.6 with its bytecode standard library and 72 native extension modules · SQLite-backed dbm/shelve and PyREPL remain available; GNU Readline and GNU dbm are not bundled. All retained Android dependencies use permissive terms.
ripgrep 15.2.0 for Android ARM64, built without PCRE2 · SHA-256 pinned in the APK with its complete statically linked dependency inventory and permissive license texts.
Includes the LLVM libc++ runtime under the University of Illinois/NCSA Open Source License.
